the perinatal outcomes of pregnancies complicated by type 1 or 2 diabetes have not improved over a 15 year period in Scotland, and that the perinatality mortality and stillbirth rate in pregnancies with type 2 are 4 times higher than those in pregnancies without diabetes.
there has been a marked increase in perinatal intervention and improved birthweight, but not in perinatal mortality or stillbirth, in pregnancies to women with pre-existing diabetes in Scotland.

despite the improvements in care, women with diabetes are not achieving optimal pregnancy outcomes.
despite the improvements in care and outcomes in the non-diabetes population, there has been little change in perinatal mortality for women with diabetes.

the perinatal outcomes for pregnancies complicated by diabetes are improving but remain suboptimal compared with pregnancies in non-diabetic women.

there is still room for improvement in the care of pregnant women with diabetes.
